_readme: THE DEMO'S COMPOSITION — which apps this box's images compose. Same format as the product's own list
(`extensions/composition.base.json` in the Forge monorepo), and deliberately NOT the same content: this
is an INSTANCE's answer, and the whole point of `image = release × list` is that the two can differ and
both be true.
THIS FILE AND `forge.lock` SAY THE SAME THING TWICE, ON PURPOSE. `forge.lock` carries the list the
images WERE BAKED FROM (the pin); this file is the list this repository MAINTAINS (the intent).
`bin/verify-composition.sh` compares the lock against what the running kernel declares — the third
party in the argument, and the only one that is a fact rather than a claim. Between an edit here and the
next bake the two disagree, and that is the honest state: the lock must never be hand-edited to promise
a list no image was built from.
★★ 02/09 — THIS LIST IS NOW THE PRODUCT'S WHOLE OOTB CATALOGUE, AND THAT IS A DECISION, NOT A DEFAULT.
It used to name SEVEN apps: the ones the two shop windows and the payment screens needed, each with its
own line of justification. That was a defensible list and it produced the wrong demo — the box that was
supposed to show what Forge CAN do shipped ten of its apps missing, and the first question asked of it
was "where did the other ones go?". So the rule for THIS box is now the opposite of the rule for a
customer's: the demo composes EVERY app the platform offers, plus the apps it wrote for itself.
· A customer's list is a CHOICE — `image = release × list` exists so a box can carry less, and the
seven-app bake proved that half of the mechanism in the field. That proof is kept in
`infra/fleet/lists/lean-instance.json` upstream, which is where a FIXTURE belongs.
· The demo's list is a SHOWCASE — an app that is not in the image has no screen, no command and no
row in the admin's Apps area, so leaving one out is hiding a capability from the person the box
exists to convince.
WHY THERE ARE NO LONGER PER-APP REASONS HERE. The old readme argued each of the seven; with the whole
catalogue on the list, arguing each of the seventeen would be re-writing the product's own documentation
into this repository, and it would go stale the day an app is added upstream. The rule replaced the
list: EVERYTHING THE PRODUCT OFFERS. What still needs a written reason is the opposite — an app the
product carries and this box does NOT compose — and that is what `notComposed` below is for.
★★ `apps` AND `instanceApps` ARE TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND THE SPLIT IS THE WHOLE POINT. `apps` names
what the PLATFORM offers and this box chose; it is the list `infra/fleet/lists/demo-instance.json` in
the monorepo mirrors, and it is the list the fleet oven can bake there because every entry is an app
that release carries. `instanceApps` names what THIS REPOSITORY WROTE — code no release of ours has
ever seen — and it reaches the bake by being copied into the build context (`bin/build-local.sh` stages
it; the oven adopts it with --instance-apps).
⚠️ AN INSTANCE APP IS ADOPTED, NEVER COMPOSED, AND PUTTING ONE ON `apps` IS A RED BUILD. The oven
refuses the collision by name — `@forge/ext-demo-gate would land on extensions/demo-gate, which this
release already carries` — and `bin/composition.guard.mjs` proves the distinction still holds before
anybody reaches the oven.
⚠️ AND THE IMAGE THAT COMES OUT IS NOT OFFERABLE, BY CONSTRUCTION. The oven stamps it, and the
platform's release gate refuses to promote such an image. That is correct and it is not a limitation of
this box: an image carrying OUR app must never be handed to anybody else. See its README and
`docs/concepts/instance-owned-apps.md` in the monorepo.
⚠️ THE COPY IN THE MONOREPO. `infra/fleet/lists/demo-instance.json` over there is this list, so the
`fleet-oven` job can bake `release × THIS list` before a release is offered. Nothing mechanical keeps
the two in step — CI does not cross repositories — so a change here is a change there, by hand, and the
symptom of forgetting is an image baked from a list this box never asked for. THE ORDER OF THE ARRAY IS
PART OF THE COMPARISON (`bin/build-local.sh` compares the two as sequences, not as sets), so copy it
verbatim. `bin/composition.guard.mjs` says so before the build does, when a checkout is at hand;
`bin/verify-composition.sh` is what catches it on the box, after the fact.
_notComposed_why: APPS THIS RELEASE CARRIES AND THIS BOX DOES NOT COMPOSE — named, with the reason, because "the demo
takes all of them" is only checkable if the exceptions are written down. `bin/composition.guard.mjs`
reads this block: every platform-origin app in the monorepo's `extensions/` must be on `apps` above OR
here with a reason, and an app that IS on the product's OOTB list may never be excused here — a
capability cannot be dropped from the showcase by prose.
Keyed by the app's DIRECTORY name under `extensions/`, which is what the guard walks.

notComposed.admin-dashboard: SOLDERED, not optional. `apps/admin` imports it directly (a non-generated source under apps/*/src), so composing it from a list would register it twice — the oven refuses it by name with rule `hand-welded`. It is in every image already, including this box's; being off this list is the opposite of being absent.
notComposed.demo-data: SOLDERED, same rule and same proof: `apps/api/src/action-registry.ts` imports its populate/wipe/adopt-legacy by hand. It is also `surface: 'platform'` — a system app the tenant does not operate — and it is what drives this box's own seeding. Off the list, in the image.

instanceApps.why: the demo's own gate: the full-screen 'Demo store' interstitial and the ribbon under it. Composed, not mounted, since Forge P1 — which is what gives it a screen on the reference storefront the Outlet runs.

the counter's two ways to pay: `pos_card` (the card machine already said yes) and `pos_pix` (the QR on the totem's screen). It is on THIS list and not on `apps` because no Forge release carries it — and it had to be written rather than reused, because `payment-reference`'s PIX mode is UNIVERSAL app config: turning it to auto-approve for the counter would take the live 'aguardando pagamento' away from the coffee store, which is a thing this demo exists to show. It is also the species' second specimen and its stronger one — `demo-gate` is UI, this is a payment DRIVER.
